question.text: The hajj, on which Mansa Musa gave away great amounts of gold, is a Muslim pilgrimage undertaken to this holiest city in Islam.
question.clue: As its citizens prepared to execute a negotiator, the Pledge of the Tree was taken outside of its walls, leading it to promptly accept the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

swap.leadin: Under the grip of its fifth president, this country was in turmoil beginning in 1980 and culminating in 2003 when it was invaded by a "coalition of the willing."
swap.text: Name this Middle Eastern country established by the British in 1921. The first ruler of this country was the Hashemite king Faisal I.
swap.answerHtml: Iraq (or Republic of Iraq or Jumhuriyat al- Iraq )
swap.clue: One autonomous region in this country was the location of a civil war between two rival political dynasties, one of which rules that region today.

question.leadin: British possessions in Asia were referred to as "East of" this structure.
question.text: Name this waterway that connected the Mediterrainian and Red Sea when it was completed in 1869.
question.clue: The Straits of Tiran were opened during a conflict over this structure that led to Anthony Eden's resignation.

swap.text: A second oil shock occurred in 1979, partially due to this country's regime change and a subsequent war with Iraq. Shah Mohammed Reza Pahlavi was deposed as leader of this country by the Ayatollah Khomeini.
swap.clue: The newspaper Al-Shiraa is best known for exposing covert US arms sales to this country.

question.leadin: Saif ad-Din Qutuz, a member of this military caste, crushed the Seventh Crusade and later defeated a Mongol army at the Battle of Ain Jalut.
question.text: Name these enslaved Muslim warriors who wielded great power throughout North Africa and the Middle East.
question.clue: They followed the furusiyya code, which includes cavalry tactics and horsemanship.

swap.leadin: This polity lost land along the Mediterranean coast to the Fatimids.
swap.text: Name this Muslim caliphate that succeeded the Umayyad. Its caliphs included Harun al-Rashid.
swap.clue: The general Abu Muslim led a revolt named for this dynasty that overthrew the Umayyad dynasty.

question.leadin: Answer some things about the exploits of Nazi special forces commander, Otto Skorzeny: ["Score-zeh-nee"].
question.text: After the war, Skorzeny served as a military advisor to this leader. Anthony Eden resigned as British Prime Minister after failing to dislodge this leader in the Suez Crisis.
question.clue: He greatly enhanced the power of the General Intelligence Directorate, and earlier, this man founded a secret organization with Abd al-Hakim Amir, Zakaria Mohieddine, and his own future successor.

swap.text: This country carried out the Entebbe raid on a Ugandan airport to rescue an hijacked airplane. It also signed the Camp David accords to give the Sinai peninsula back to nearby Egypt.
swap.clue: This country's early "Austerity" period led it to sign a reparations agreement with West Germany under its first leader David Ben-Gurion.

question.leadin: Many graduates from the then declining Academy of Gondishapur were hired to work at this institution.
question.text: Name this institution of learning which was greatly expanded by al-Ma'mun. Much of our knowledge regarding this Baghdad-based institution comes from al-Tabari.
question.answerHtml: House of Wisdom [or Bayt al-Ḥikmah; or Grand Library of Baghdad]
question.clue: The creator of algebra worked as an astronomer here, and it was founded as a private library by al-Mansur or Harun al-Rashid before being opened to the public.

swap.leadin: Members of this group likely kidnapped and tortured to death William R. Higgins, who was overseeing a UN peacekeeping effort in 1985.
swap.text: Identify this Shi'a militia group that receives backing from Iran. Hassan Nasrallah has headed this group since 1992.
swap.answerHtml: Hezbollah [or Hizbullah; or Hizballah; prompt on Party of God; prompt on Party of Allah]
swap.clue: Led by Hassan Nasrallah, and given major funding by Iran, this group's 2006 kidnapping of Israeli soldiers sparked a brief war between Israel and the country which it controls large parts of.

question.text: Abu Simbel is the site of two temples that were created during the reign of Ramses II, but had to be moved to higher ground in 1964 to avoid flooding as a result of the creation of this dam.
question.clue: In 1956 John Foster Dulles announced that the US was withdrawing funding, following the Soviets offering over one billion dollars in funding.

swap.leadin: Dhu Nuwas ("dhoo nu-WAS") violently converted much of this modern-day country's Christian population to Judaism before committing suicide by riding his horse into the sea.
swap.text: Name this modern-day country whose Jewish population can be traced back to the kingdom of Himyar. The earlier kingdom of Saba' in this country exported frankincense and myrrh.
swap.clue: Muhammad al-Badr was deposed as king of its Mutawakkilite Kingdom provoking a 1962 Civil War.

question.leadin: In the United States, the names of certain foods are often changed due to foreign policy.
question.text: Bob Ney renamed French fries to "freedom fries" due to French opposition to this U.S. action, which Michael Ledeen argued was justified due to a dictator's purchases of yellowcake uranium from Niger.
question.answerHtml: invading Iraq [or descriptive answers indicating war with Iraq; or the Iraq War; or Operation Iraqi Freedom; or the Second Gulf War; or Second Persian Gulf War; prompt on Gulf War or Persian Gulf War]

swap.text: This caliph sent the general Amr ibn al-'As to capture that fortress at Babylon, whereupon he founded Fustat. This caliph, who succeeded Abu Bakr and preceded Uthman, was given the title al-Farooq by Muhammad.
swap.clue: The last Sassanian king, Yazdegird III, was murdered by a brigand after his forces were defeated by this caliph's force at Qadisiyya. His creation of the qadi judgeship and divan pension system is considered the beginning of Islamic jurisprudence.

question.leadin: Along with its country's security forces, this organization is prominently represented in the Ergenekon.
question.text: Name this organization whose Counter-Guerrilla was part of Operation Gladio. It has a record of launching coups to impose the secularism of the Six Arrows.
question.answerHtml: Turkish army [or Turkish military, Turkish armed forces; antiprompt on answers with a “non-army branch of the Turkish armed forces”; do not accept “Turkish secret police”, “Turkish police”, Turkish ]

swap.leadin: Adherents of this sect argue that the death of the man who names it was faked by his father Ja'far al-Sadiq.
swap.text: Name this Islamic sect. The successful proselytization efforts by several da'i missionaries of this sect led rival authorities to issue the Baghdad Manifesto to try to disprove genealogical claims made by a dynasty of this sect.
swap.answerHtml: Isma’ilism [or al-ʾIsmāʿīlīyah; prompt on, BUT DO NOT OTHERWISE REVEAL, Shi’a]
swap.clue: Rashid al-Din's canonical Mongol history drew on Juvayni's History of the World Conqueror, which portrays this sect as heretical and praises Hulagu's campaigns against it in Qazvin.

question.text: This Lt. Colonel of the Israeli Defense Force led the operation and was its only Israeli casualty.

swap.leadin: Answer some things about military blunders of the Umayyad Caliphate.
swap.text: In this 750 AD battle, an Umayyad army under Marwan II was defeated by an insurgent force of Abbasids under as-Saffah at a tributary of the Tigris. The battle at this river ended the Umayyad dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of the Zab River [or the Great Zab] 10

question.text: This golden-voiced friend of Muhammad was born into slavery as the son of Ethiopian princess captured during the Abyssinian attempt to destroy the Kaaba during the Year of the Elephant. He was later freed and became the first muezzin.
question.answerHtml: Bilal ibn Rabah [or Bilal al-Habashi; or Bilal ibn Riyah; prompt on “ibn Rabah” or “al- Habashi” or “ibn Riyah”]

swap.leadin: Name these participants of the Third Crusade.
swap.text: The reign as King of Jerusalem of this bellicose cousin of Frederick Barbarossa, who defended Tyre from Saladin during the Third Crusade, ended after he was assassinated in broad daylight.
swap.answerHtml: Conrad of Montferrat [or Conrad I of Jerusalem; prompt on Conrad]
